goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weed check` judges a diff and may block; `weed scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weed guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weed bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop. Make the checks below pass, honestly.
Nobody reviews your prose, only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
The rules that block by default, because each names a shape no honest change has: a deleted test, an added skip or focus, a stub in production code, a secret, an edited guardrail, and a conflict marker (G1, already live on check-face). Each lands as a failing fixture first in TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Rust and Go, then the detector, and each has a neighbour fixture where it must stay silent. A rule detects a shape, never a vendor or a product name.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/rules-block.tend2.html) is your full context, read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) C1 fires at block level on the harness hook configs (`.claude/settings*.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `.codex/*`), on `.githooks/*` other than weed's own bundle, on `weed.toml`, and on a hunk touching the hard-limits section of `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`; it stays silent on `.github/CODEOWNERS`, on a hunk elsewhere in `AGENTS.md`, and on a GitHub workflow file · evidence expected at: tests/rule_c1.rs
- (code) X1 fires on a known-prefix token in any file and applies its key-like-name heuristic only to files classified as source code, so a `name = value` shape inside a markup attribute or a line of markdown prose about credentials stays silent while the same shape in ts, py, rs and go source still fires · evidence expected at: tests/rule_x1.rs
- (code) S1 stays silent on a Python method whose body is an ellipsis inside a `Protocol` or an abstract class, where the ellipsis declares a type rather than defers an implementation, and still fires on an ellipsis body in a concrete function or class · evidence expected at: tests/rule_s1.rs
- (code) T1 counts a test case generated in a loop or a table as present, so cases that move from static declarations into a `for` around `it`, a `t.Run` in a range, a `parametrize` list or a macro-generated `#[test]` are not reported as deleted, in ts, py, rs and go, while a case that leaves the file altogether still is · evidence expected at: tests/rule_t1.rs
- (code) C3 warns by default on a change to a file under `.github/workflows/`, fire and silent fixtures alike, and a repository that names workflow paths under `[guardrails] paths` in `weed.toml` gets them at block level; the catalogue, `docs/rules.md` and `weed rules` carry C3 as a warn rule with what/why/next in its message · evidence expected at: tests/rule_c3.rs

## Definition of done, verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/rules-block.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload b30fe9d88813 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

## Already tried (do not repeat)
- 2026-09-05 rule files are `src/core/rules/check/<id>.rs`, one per rule, registered in `src/core/rules/check/mod.rs`; scan rules get their own registry so the two faces never share a file
- 2026-09-05 T2 (assertions dropped) is on rules-tests although it blocks by default: its count depends on per-language assertion vocabularies that the tests loop owns, and the block set here is the one the umbrella loop names as unambiguous
- 2026-09-05 X1's prefix list overlaps pleach's hygiene gate on purpose: both are the same shapes, and weed is the one that runs where pleach does not
- 2026-09-05 built by pleach node `rules-block` (claude/opus, codex audit) in one attempt, 41 minutes, landed by hand after `pleach land` met the hardening loop's change to the git seam; merged as both readings (a NUL byte is a binary blob and reads as nothing, anything else reads as text with stray bytes replaced). T1 counts cases from the reader's test shape on both sides; T3, S1 and X1 read through a syntax mask so a marker inside a string or a comment says nothing; the secret and marker fixtures use placeholders the harness expands, so the repository carries no credential and no marker
- 2026-09-05 conductor correction, fixed inline and re-verified: the worker concluded that weed must refuse its own hook installation under C1 (`.githooks/*` is a guardrail path) and made adoption a commit that skips the hooks, which the hooks face denies outright. C1 now recognises weed's own bundle byte for byte (`guard::is_own_bundle`: the binary its marker names and the branches its exec line protects, handed back to `guard::script`), so adopting weed goes through the gate the hooks run, and a bundle that differs by one byte is a guardrail edit again. `tests/rule_c1.rs` pins both halves; the guard tests adopt weed with ordinary commits
- 2026-09-05 left open, for calibration: `weed check` on weed's own tree reports the T3 and S1 fixtures, which are meant to look dishonest. A per-path specimen exclusion in `weed.toml` is the fix; a fixture that stops carrying a skip stops being a fixture
- 2026-09-05 cape-town on C1's self-recognition: byte for byte on weed's own bundle is the right shape; when the stem later generates that bundle, the pin moves to the stem's output. Never widen it to a path match
- 2026-09-06 calibration over 635 real commits (docs/calibration-2026-09.md, `Where weed was wrong`) found three shapes worth their own checks, added above: seven of nine block-level false positives are X1 reading `name = value` in a css class attribute or a markdown sentence; S1 calls a Python `Protocol` method with an ellipsis body a stub; T1 counts only statically declared cases, so a case generated in a loop reads as one that vanished. Calibration now needs this loop, so the next run measures the fixed rules
- 2026-09-06 cape-town's C1 ruling, after calibration showed 42 of 71 blocks were honest workflow edits: split it. Block-level C1 is the constitution tier, the agent's own guardrails, harness hook configs, `.githooks/*`, `weed.toml`, the hard-limits sections of `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. GitHub workflow files are by-laws, edited legitimately all the time, and move to C3 at warn, promoted to block per repository under `[guardrails] paths`. The C1 check above is reworded to the split, which voids its stamp on purpose

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file, check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green, it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Probe/scratch files (toolchain checks, experiments) go in `.loop-scratch/` only, it is never collected; scratch files elsewhere pollute the delivery.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root, what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
